recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is and do not change ResearchSubject.status for FHIR-14163. Future work, if any, should be handled under later ResearchSubject.subjectState or THO terminology issues rather than this STU3 status-binding issue.
issue_request: FHIR-14163 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 BR&R change request to update ResearchSubject so ResearchSubject.status used a vetted ResearchSubjectStatus value set for subject progression; Jira records that the change was made and published in the Dec 2017 ballot.
initial_application: The original application is visible in git history: 51ac19819f8117a5a0c2827b0df972681ba430d9 updated the ResearchSubject.status row in source/status-codes.xml to the vetted subject-progression list, and b17e23b77e7eeef1a16b7e68c65dd54605f822cd updated the ResearchSubject resource spreadsheet in the same GF14163 Dec 2017 work.
additional_context: ResearchSubject is active in the current build via source/fhir.ini. Later Published BR&R issues FHIR-31657 and FHIR-31689 approved progress modeling and explicitly restricted ResearchSubject.status to publication status. R6 work then replaced progress with subjectState and moved the subject-state binding to THO, with FHIR-49254 changing subjectState.code binding strength to example for flexibility.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source correctly binds ResearchSubject.status to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/publication-status and represents subject progression through ResearchSubject.subjectState.code bound to http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/research-subject-state. Reapplying the old ResearchSubjectStatus binding to ResearchSubject.status would conflict with later final decisions.
